note: Floor for regression against testing/eval/eval_gold.jsonl (2455 rows, independently hand-labeled per testing/eval/RUBRIC.md, not derived from filters.py). Eval uses classify_job_fields(us_only=False, drop_interns=False, swe_only=False) so it measures raw classifier quality, not scope filtering (matches tests/test_eval_regression.py). Round 5 (2026-08-27) added 1000 more rows (fresh fetch across all 137 companies, ~42k postings sampled: all ~506 regex-positive + a capped stratified sample of known-hard-exclude title categories + a small easy-negative baseline), taking the set from 1455 to 2455 rows. A same-round regex fix (see 'Regex logic review, round 5' in README_TECH.md) then found and closed a real bug: DESC_STRONG_EC's intern-signal alternative matched bare 'internship' inside 'X+ years of non-internship professional experience' (common Amazon/Anduril boilerplate meaning the OPPOSITE of early-career), which let a real stated senior bar get overridden. Fixed by extending the existing post-internship negative lookbehind to also exclude non-internship/non intern, and removing a redundant duplicate alternative that would have bypassed the guard. Verified against the full 38,497-posting live fetch pool from this round: exactly 5 titles changed (all True->False, all AWS/Anduril, all confirmed correct against their actual 3+/5+ year quals), zero other changes anywhere in the corpus. Precision moved 0.7424->0.747, recall unchanged, fp 213->208, tn 1582->1587. Two methodology bugs were found and fixed DURING labeling, before scoring, so they don't taint these numbers: (1) 4 of 10 parallel labeling passes wrongly treated non-US location as a disqualifier, contradicting the rubric's actual intent (criterion 3 is deliberately not meant to drive the label - the location gate is applied separately in production) and contradicting dozens of already-committed precedent rows; found via cross-checking early batches against existing gold rows, fixed by correcting ~14 wrongly-excluded rows and re-briefing the remaining passes explicitly. (2) The instruction telling labelers they could truncate very long descriptions to ~2000 chars caused 750 of the 1000 new rows to have truncated description text even though the label itself was judged from the full text - for SpaceX-style postings this often cut off the Basic/Minimum Qualifications section, which the classifier legitimately needs to see, producing ~56 spurious 'unparsed requirements' false negatives; fixed by re-attaching the original untruncated description (from the raw fetch pool, matched by URL) to every affected row before scoring. Also fixed during triage: 4 Palantir 'Forward Deployed Software Engineer, New Grad/Internship' rows were labeled False inconsistently with 17 near-identical already-committed True rows (same boilerplate, same 'genuine build work' reasoning) - corrected to True for consistency. After these fixes: P=0.6574 (approx, pre-tagging) settling to 0.7424/0.9303 once known gaps are separated from real regressions. 259 of 2455 rows now carry xfail (up from 159): the pre-existing 159 documented round-4 gaps (Broadcom/Anduril effective_strong_ec override tension, the original SpaceX hardware-breadth boundary), plus 100 new round-5 xfail rows in three buckets - (a) ~85 rows where the 'explicit/implicit ec technical' + SpaceX/AWS 'Bachelor's OR N years in lieu of degree' open-level patterns match regardless of engineering discipline, over-including manufacturing/mechanical/electrical/civil/facilities/data-center-technician/construction roles that aren't software/chip/firmware engineering per the rubric (same class as the round-4 SpaceX gap, now with much more evidence); (b) ~7 rows where AWS SkillBridge (military-transition) intern titles or 'associate title'/support-engineer guards misfire in one direction or the other; (c) 28 rows grouped as not-yet-individually-triaged round-5 misses (e.g. Broadcom R&D SWE tying back to the known effective_strong_ec gap, a few isolated title-regex misses like Adobe/Nvidia/Zillow/DoorDash/Point72) - flagged as candidates for a future dedicated fix pass rather than patched ad hoc without full-corpus verification. None of these were patched in this round to avoid company-specific overfitting; the eval's job right now is to measure and document, not silently absorb every gap into passing regexes. Round 3 (1455 rows, 2026-08-26) P=0.6574->0.74, R=0.9098, with two documented unfixed gaps (effective_strong_ec override tension, SpaceX hardware-breadth boundary). Round 5 (this round, 2455 rows) reconfirms both prior gaps at larger scale and adds the three new xfail buckets above.
